STEP 1 - Scene: A top-down photo of a single small food item on a white square plate. It looks like a cross-section slice of corn on the cob.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 24 cm wide, so its area is roughly 3.14 x 12^2 ≈ 450 cm² (a bit less because of the rounded corners, call it ~430 cm²). The plate spans about 345 px, so 1 cm ≈ 14 px.

STEP 3 - Items: One corn slice (a cob cross-section with kernels). There is no sauce or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: The slice is about 100 px across, which is about 7 cm. Its area is 3.14 x 3.5^2 ≈ 38 cm², or about 9% of the plate. Food covers only ~9% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The slice looks about 2.5 cm thick, so 38 x 2.5 ≈ 95 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A cob has a dense core, so I use a density of about 0.6 g/ml, giving ~57 g. The slice may be smaller than that, since the ~7 cm diameter is a generous reading, so I settle on about 55 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Corn on the cob is about 96 kcal/100 g, so 55 g gives about 53 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single corn slice of about 55 g and about 53 kcal is plausible for what is visible.
